paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God raised Joseph from the dungeon to the palace, and Pharaoh saw it for what it was. Pharaoh told Joseph, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you." (Genesis 41:39) The wisdom wasn't Joseph's own, because it came from God.

Now look at what Joseph does with the new power. He doesn't throw a party for himself, he gets to work, storing up the food before the hungry years come (Genesis 41:48). When the famine hits, "there was food throughout the land of Egypt." (Genesis 41:54) Preparing in the good years fed people in the bad ones, and that's a good word for anybody with an oven.

Joseph names his second son Ephraim and says, "God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction." (Genesis 41:52) I think Joseph saw God's hand in the hard years and in the good ones. So when you're in your own hard place, baker, keep your eyes on God and your hands busy, because God can bring good out of the hardest ground. And this story isn't over yet.
